subproblem.title: Bounded subsets of a k-frame span have finite H^k-measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let g = (g_1, …, g_k) (g : Fin k → Euclid P) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P with span G := span{g_1, …, g_k}; H^k := μHE[k]. Then every bounded set E ⊆ G (Bornology.IsBounded E) has finite H^k-measure: μHE[k] E ≠ ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (g : Fin k → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ g → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), E ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) : Set (Euclid P)) → Bornology.IsBounded E → μHE[k] E ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof.

Uses frame_measure (ii), the closed-box half of Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_frame_measure: for every r > 0, H^k({t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i}) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k).

1. Since E is bounded, E ⊆ closedBall(0, ρ) for some ρ ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put r := max(ρ, 0) + 1, so that r > 0 and ρ ≤ r.
2. Let t ∈ E. Then t ∈ G, because E ⊆ G. For each i, Cauchy–Schwarz (abs_real_inner_le_norm) and ‖g_i‖ = 1 (orthonormality) give |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ ‖g_i‖·‖t‖ = ‖t‖ ≤ ρ ≤ r. Hence E ⊆ Box_r := {t : t ∈ G ∧ ∀ i, |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r}.
3. By frame_measure (ii) with this r > 0, H^k(Box_r) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k), which is finite (ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top).
4. By monotonicity of the measure (measure_mono), H^k(E) ≤ H^k(Box_r) < ∞, so μHE[k] E ≠ ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: E ⊆ closedBall(0, ρ). With r = max(ρ, 0) + 1 > 0, Cauchy–Schwarz and ‖g_i‖ = 1 give E ⊆ {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i}.
frame_measure (ii) gives this closed box H^k-measure ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k) < ∞; monotonicity finishes.

audit.reason: The type exactly states finiteness for every bounded subset of the frame span. No measurability assumption is needed: enclosure in a positive-radius closed frame box and measure monotonicity suffice. The supplied proof correctly uses orthonormality and the exact closed-box conclusion of frame_measure. Its explicit citation creates the inherited prerequisite, so the empty sibling-dependency list is correct and acyclic.
